children: Microsoft
has decided not to expand a major AI computing agreement with UK startup Nscale, walking away from an option that could have been worth
tens of billions of dollars

The decision affects additional capacity at a Texas data center where Microsoft already has a contract with Nscale. Importantly, the existing agreement remains in place. Microsoft's decision not to exercise the expansion option was made several months ago, before Nscale filed for an IPO in September.
The companies had previously agreed for Nscale to deploy around
200,000 Nvidia AI chips
across data centers in the U.S. and Europe.
Nscale disclosed in its IPO filing that statements of work signed with Microsoft between September 2025 and April 2026 were worth up to about
$43.8 billion through 2033
, excluding optional extensions.
The rejected Texas expansion would reportedly have covered about
500 megawatts of additional capacity
, potentially adding billions of dollars of future revenue for Nscale. The startup now needs to find other customers for that capacity.
That adds to a growing list of execution challenges.

Microsoft previously pulled out of plans to anchor Nscale's flagship data-center project in Essex after power-connection delays pushed expected supply into the 2030s. Nscale is also developing a massive West Virginia campus tied to a potential
$45 billion Anthropic deal
, but that project faces substantial financing and construction requirements.
Still, Nscale says the Microsoft decision does
not
affect the roughly
$103 billion of total contract value
disclosed in its IPO filing. The company is already in talks with other major customers for the unused Texas capacity.
Investor Takeaway
I think the most important point is that this does
not necessarily mean Microsoft is pulling back from AI spending broadly
The company is declining an optional expansion with one infrastructure provider. Its existing Nscale Texas contract remains intact.
That makes this look more like a
project-specific discipline story
than clear evidence of weakening AI demand.
For Nscale, however, the timing is difficult.
The company is trying to support a planned IPO reportedly valued around
$35 billion
, while investors are already questioning the financing needs and execution risk surrounding AI infrastructure businesses.
For investors, the key things to watch are

whether Nscale quickly replaces Microsoft with another customer, whether Anthropic expands its relationship, financing progress in West Virginia, and whether Microsoft makes similar cuts with other AI infrastructure partners
One rejected option does not break the AI spending boom.
But for Nscale, it raises the pressure considerably.

title: Microsoft Just Walked Away From a Huge AI Deal
